key_insight: Mechanistic interpretability can predict and reduce web-agent hallucinations, but explaining their underlying causes remains difficult.
engineering_relevance: Probe-based steering could help prevent invalid web actions, but prompt sensitivity and disruption of valid actions limit deployment reliability.
method: Analyze Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct interacting with live websites.
Train a linear probe on last-prompt-token activations to predict hallucinations before generation.
Steer activations along the probe direction and investigate circuits underlying failures.
evidence_signal: The probe achieves 0.80 AUC, while steering corrects 85% of hallucinations but disrupts 7% of valid actions.
watch_item: A minor change in action formatting substantially weakens steering, indicating that the intervention may not generalize across prompt formats.
paper_title: Can Mechanistic Interpretability Help Explain LLM Agent Failures? A Case Study on Web Element Hallucination
